defects.description: The requested character limit is passed directly to String.prototype.slice in UTF-16 code units, so truncation can return a lone surrogate instead of valid Unicode.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { truncate } from "./src/truncate.js"; const output = truncate("😀😀😀", 1); const roundTrip = new TextDecoder().decode(new TextEncoder().encode(output)); console.log(JSON.stringify({ output, roundTrip, equal: output === roundTrip }));'

defects.why_missed: The happy suite uses only single-unit text, so no tested character can be split at a UTF-16 boundary.

traps.description: Exactly one trailing LF is stripped before truncation, as the README documents.
